correctness.rationale: For \(n=pq\), the equation is exactly \(4\sigma(pq+1)=5(p+1)(q+1)\). The even-number divisor lower bound implies \((p-5)(q-5)<24\). It excludes \(p\ge11\) and reduces \(p=7\) to two failures. For \(p=5\), either \(\sigma(t)=t+2\) for odd \(t>1\), impossible, or the divisor lower bound contradicts the required equality. For \(p=3\), a sharper bound and prime congruences give exactly the stated equivalent parameterization. For \(p=2\), a factorization proof yields \(4\mid\sigma(2q+1)\), whence \(16\mid q+1\). Direct witnesses and finite corroboration were checked.

value.rationale: The question is motivated by the natural exact equation between a one-step divisor-sum increase and the divisor mean, recorded publicly for twenty-five years. The theorem excludes all semiprimes with smaller prime at least five without any size cutoff, isolates two rigid congruence classes, and converts the nonempty odd branch into an exact sigma equation on an odd progression. This is a substantial unbounded structural sieve, not an arbitrary parameter slice or finite recomputation.
